mainTopic: The end of the שעיר המשתלח's journey on יום כפור: the booths and escorts, the split red strip and its history, and whether one may benefit from the goat's limbs.
overview: This עמוד finishes the משנה about the last stage of the שעיר המשתלח on יום כפור. Booths along the 12-מיל route offered the sender food and water, and people escorted him from booth to booth. At the cliff he tied half of a red strip (לשון של זהורית) to a rock and half between the goat's horns, then pushed the goat backward off the cliff. He waited under the last booth until dark, and the משנה ends with a מחלוקת about when his clothes become טמא. The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue about the number of booths and the distance. All three agree the escorts relied on an עירוב, and the line about the last escort staying back is shown to follow רבי מאיר. The גמרא then explains several points. The food was offered only for peace of mind. The strip was split so the sender would stay focused on the goat and still be able to see the sign. Two traditions describe how the strip used to hang at the אולם, with the פסוק 'כשנים כשלג ילבינו' as a hint that red turning white means כפרה. Finally, רב and שמואל disagree about whether one may benefit from the goat's limbs, and the explanation of their reasoning continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The distance to the cliff and the food and water at each booth
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the total distance of the route as 90 ריס, which equals 12 מיל. At every booth, people offer the sender food and water.
steps.simpleTranslation: The trip was ninety ריס, with seven and a half ריס in each מיל. At every single booth they say to him: Here is food, and here is water.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues describing the route from ירושלים to the cliff. It gives the distance and tells us that every booth offered the sender food and water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ninety ריס divided by seven and a half ריס per מיל comes out to 12 מיל, which matches the view of רבי מאיר in the ברייתא later on. The food and water are offered even though it is יום כפור. Just knowing he is allowed to eat if he truly needs to helps the sender handle the long, hard walk.

keyTerms.meaning: A unit of distance. There are 7.5 ריס in one מיל.
A unit of distance equal to 2,000 אמות.
Here this means a booth or hut set up along the road, not the סוכה of סוכות.

steps.confusionAlert: The 90 ריס is the TOTAL distance from ירושלים to the cliff, not the distance between each booth. The math works out: 90 ÷ 7.5 = 12 מיל.

phrases.english: Ninety ris (total distance),
seven and a half for each mil (so 12 mil in all).

phrases.aramaic: עַל כׇּל סוּכָּה וְסוּכָּה אוֹמְרִין לוֹ:
phrases.english: At each and every booth they say to him:
Here is food, and here is water.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּשְׁעִים רִיס, שִׁבְעָה וּמֶחֱצָה לְכׇל מִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of the route from the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The route is 12 מיל, and at every booth the sender is offered food and water.

steps.title: Escorting the sender from booth to booth
steps.stepSummary: People escort the sender from one booth to the next. The man from the last booth does not go all the way to the cliff. He watches from far away.
steps.simpleTranslation: They escort him from booth to booth, except for the last of them. That last one does not reach the cliff with him. Instead he stands at a distance and watches what he does.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us the sender was never left alone along the route. The only exception is the last stretch, where the escort watches from a distance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The escorts keep the sender company along the way. The last escort cannot walk all the way to the cliff, but he still watches, so that someone sees the מצוה being done correctly. On יום כפור there are שבת-like limits on how far a person may walk, and the ברייתא in step 6 explains that the escorts managed this by relying on an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The cliff from which the goat was pushed.

phrases.english: And they escort him from booth to booth,
except for the last one among them,
who does not reach the cliff with him,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עוֹמֵד מֵרָחוֹק וְרוֹאֶה אֶת מַעֲשָׂיו.
phrases.english: rather, he stands at a distance and watches his actions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the escort system to the booth setup described in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sender is escorted from booth to booth. The last escort watches from a distance instead of going to the cliff.

steps.title: Tying the red strip and pushing the goat off the cliff
steps.stepSummary: At the cliff, the sender splits a red strip of wool. He ties half to a rock and half between the goat's horns, then pushes the goat backward so it rolls down.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would he do? He divided a strip of red wool. Half was tied to the rock, and half was tied between the goat's two horns. He pushed it backward, and it rolled and went down.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks what the sender actually did at the cliff and then answers. He ties the red strip and pushes the goat over the edge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'מה היה עושה' is not a challenge. It is the משנה's own way of moving to the next part of the description. The red strip connects to the famous idea that it would turn white as a sign that the sins were forgiven. Splitting it lets him keep half on the rock where he can see it.

phrases.english: What would he do?
phrases.notes: The משנה's own transition question, not a challenge.

phrases.english: He divides a strip of crimson wool:
half of it tied to the rock,
and half of it tied between its two horns.
And he pushed it backward,
and it rolls and goes down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the journey to what happens at the cliff itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The red strip is split between the rock and the goat's horns, and the goat is pushed backward off the cliff.

steps.title: The goat is destroyed and the sender waits until dark
steps.stepSummary: Before the goat gets even halfway down, it is torn limb from limb. The sender then sits under the last booth until nightfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: It would not reach halfway down the mountain before it was torn into pieces. He came and sat under the last booth until it got dark.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us what happened to the goat and what the sender did afterward. He did not go home right away but waited at the last booth until dark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goat is completely destroyed very quickly, which finishes the מצוה of sending it to עזאזל. The sender waits because walking back to ירושלים would mean going past the walking limits (תחום) of יום כפור. Once it gets dark, the day is over and he may return.

keyTerms.meaning: Limb by limb, meaning torn into pieces.
Until it gets dark, at the end of the day.

phrases.english: And it would not reach halfway down the mountain
before it was made into limbs upon limbs (torn apart).

phrases.aramaic: בָּא וְיָשַׁב לוֹ תַּחַת סוּכָּה אַחֲרוֹנָה
phrases.english: He came and sat himself under the last booth
until it got dark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the result of the push and the sender's next move.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The goat is destroyed before it reaches halfway down, and the sender stays at the last booth until dark.

steps.title: When the sender's clothes become impure
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says the sender's clothes become טמא once he leaves the wall of ירושלים. רבי שמעון says it only happens when he pushes the goat off the cliff.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when do his clothes become impure? From when he goes out past the wall of ירושלים. רבי שמעון says: from the moment he pushes it off the cliff.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a מחלוקת about the exact moment the sender's clothes become טמא. The תורה says the sender must wash his clothes, which is why they are considered טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is what makes him an official 'sender'. The תנא קמא says it starts when he leaves the city with the goat. רבי שמעון says it starts only at the final act of pushing it off the cliff. Either way, he is the person the תורה says needs to immerse his clothes. They only disagree about when that status begins.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with a מחלוקת. For the תנא קמא, the clothes become טמא when the sender leaves the wall of ירושלים. For רבי שמעון, it happens only when he pushes the goat off the cliff.

phrases.english: And from when does it make clothes impure?
From when he goes out beyond the wall of Jerusalem.
Rabbi Shimon says:
From the moment of his pushing it off the cliff.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from describing what happened to a halachic question about טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: the clothes become טמא from leaving the wall of ירושלים. רבי שמעון: from the moment the goat is pushed off the cliff.

steps.title: A three-way dispute over the number of booths and the distance
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings three views. רבי מאיר says 10 booths and 12 מיל. רבי יהודה says 9 booths and 10 מיל. רבי יוסי says 5 booths and 10 מיל. All agree the escorts relied on an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: There were ten booths and twelve מיל, according to רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: nine booths and ten מיל. רבי יוסי says: five booths and ten מיל. And all of them worked through an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by bringing a ברייתא that argues about the setup of the route described in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's 12 מיל fits רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי say the route was shorter, and רבי יוסי says far fewer booths were needed. All three agree that the escorts could walk between booths on יום כפור only because they set up an עירוב תחומין beforehand.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught. This introduces a ברייתא.
Here this means עירוב תחומין, which extends how far a person may walk on שבת or יום טוב.
These are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.confusionAlert: The עירוב here is NOT the עירוב חצרות used for carrying. It is עירוב תחומין, which lets a person walk farther than the usual 2,000 אמות limit.

phrases.english: GEMARA. The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: עֶשֶׂר סוּכּוֹת, וּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מִילִין הָיוּ,
phrases.english: There were ten booths and twelve mil,
the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: תֵּשַׁע סוּכּוֹת, וַעֲשָׂרָה מִילִין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: nine booths and ten mil.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: חָמֵשׁ סוּכּוֹת, וַעֲשָׂרָה מִילִין הָיוּ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: there were five booths and ten mil.
And all of them were by means of an eiruv.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עֶשֶׂר סוּכּוֹת, וּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מִילִין הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins and brings a ברייתא about the booth setup described in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a three-way מחלוקת on the number of booths and the distance. All three agree the escorts relied on an עירוב.

steps.title: Elazar's claim that two booths would be enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי reports that his son אלעזר told him something. If the escorts rely on an עירוב, then even two booths would be enough for 10 מיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: My son אלעזר told me: If it works through an עירוב, I could make it work with even two booths for ten מיל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי quotes his son אלעזר, who pushes the עירוב idea further. If everyone uses an עירוב, the number of booths can be cut down to just two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an עירוב a person may walk 2 מיל (4,000 אמות) in one direction. People from ירושלים walk 2 מיל, and people from booth one come out 2 מיל to meet them. Others from booth one walk 2 מיל toward booth two, whose people come out 2 מיל to meet them. Booth two is then just 2 מיל from the cliff, so two booths cover 10 מיל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the number of booths depends entirely on how far escorts may walk with an עירוב. It challenges whether even רבי יוסי's five booths were really necessary.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
Elazar my son told me:
If it is by means of an eiruv,

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹלְנִי לַעֲשׂוֹת אֲפִילּוּ שְׁתֵּי סוּכּוֹת וַעֲשָׂרָה מִילִין.
phrases.english: I could make even two booths for ten mil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: סָח לִי אֶלְעָזָר בְּנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the shared עירוב assumption from step 6 and argues that even fewer booths would be needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the escorts rely on an עירוב, two booths are enough to cover 10 מיל.

steps.title: Which view matches the teaching that the last escort stays back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא saying the last escort does not reach the cliff. It asks which of the three views from step 6 this fits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this ברייתא follow: 'except for the last one of them, who did not reach the cliff with him, but stands from far away and watches what he does'? Whose view is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the escorts and asks which תנא it matches. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 brought three opinions about how many booths there were and how far they reached. This ברייתא says the last escort could not walk all the way to the cliff. That only makes sense if the last booth was too far from the cliff, so the גמרא wants to know whose numbers produce that result.

keyTerms.meaning: The cliff where the goat is pushed off
The last one of them (the escort from the final booth)

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that which was taught:
except for the last one of them
who did not reach the cliff with him
rather, he stands from a distance
and watches his actions.
In accordance with whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties a new ברייתא to the three-way argument about booths and distances.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's count of booths and distance fits a last escort who cannot reach the cliff.

steps.title: It follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא matches רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר spreads 10 booths over 12 מיל. Under his numbers, the last booth is too far from the cliff for its escort to walk the whole way. So that escort can only stand at a distance and watch.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who holds 10 booths and 12 מיל

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, because his larger distance leaves the last booth too far from the cliff.

steps.title: At every booth they offer food and water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: at each booth the people tell the sender that food and water are ready for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: At each and every booth they say to him: Here is food, and here is water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to set up its explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is יום כיפור, so eating is normally forbidden. Still, the people at every booth offer the sender food and water. The גמרא will explain why they bother.

keyTerms.meaning: A booth along the path to the cliff

phrases.english: At each and every booth
they say to him:
Here is food and here is water.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כׇּל סוּכָּה וְסוּכָּה אוֹמְרִים לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At each booth the sender is offered food and water.

steps.title: No one ever needed the food, but having it calms a person
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that no sender ever actually ate. The offer was made because a person who knows food is available feels less hungry.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: No person ever needed this. But a person who has bread in his basket is not like a person who has no bread in his basket.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא explains the משנה's line about food and water. The offer was for peace of mind, not because anyone used it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone with no food nearby worries about it, and that worry makes the hunger feel worse. Knowing that food is right there makes the fast much easier to bear. So the offer helped even though no one ever took it.

keyTerms.meaning: Bread in his basket: having food on hand

steps.whatToRemember: The food and water were never eaten. Just knowing they are available eases the strain of fasting.

phrases.english: It was taught:
No person ever needed this,
but it is not the same:
one who has bread in his basket
compared to one who has no bread in his basket.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: מֵעוֹלָם לֹא הוּצְרַךְ אָדָם לְכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the משנה quoted in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The offer is made for peace of mind, even though no one ever used it.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: he splits the red strip
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה saying the sender divides the red strip of wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would he do? He divides a strip of red wool.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about splitting the red strip. This sets up the two questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As described in step 3, half the strip goes on the rock and half goes between the goat's horns. The גמרא is about to ask why the strip is split instead of all tied in one place.

phrases.english: What would he do?
He divides a strip of crimson wool.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֶה הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה חוֹלֵק לָשׁוֹן שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's description from step 3 in order to analyze it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The red strip is divided into two parts.

steps.title: Why not tie all of it to the rock?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the whole strip is not simply tied to the rock.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him tie all of it to the rock!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the split: tying the whole strip to the rock seems simpler.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strip is there to turn white as a sign that the sins are forgiven. Tying it all in one place on the rock would seem to do that job, so the split looks unnecessary.

phrases.english: Let him tie all of it to the rock?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's practice of splitting the strip.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of splitting the strip.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One strip on the rock would show forgiveness just as well, so splitting it seems pointless.

steps.title: If it whitens too early, he may forget to push the goat
steps.stepSummary: The מצוה is to push the goat. If the strip on the rock whitened first, he might relax and never push it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the מצוה is with the goat, perhaps the strip would turn white early, and he would feel at ease.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: tying everything to the rock risks the sender feeling finished before he pushes the goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pushing the goat off the cliff is the actual מצוה. If the strip on the rock turned white before the push, he might think the job was done and skip it. Tying half on the goat keeps his attention on the goat, so he remembers to push it.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה is done with the goat (pushing it)
His mind is put at ease

phrases.english: Since the מצוה is with the goat,
perhaps it will turn white early
and his mind will be settled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tying it all to the rock would be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some must go on the goat so the sender stays focused on pushing it.

steps.title: Then why not tie all of it to the horns?
steps.stepSummary: If the goat is the focus, the גמרא asks why the whole strip is not tied between its horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him tie all of it between its horns!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further: if the strip belongs on the goat, put all of it there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 14 explains why some of the strip goes on the goat. It does not yet explain why any of it stays on the rock.

phrases.english: Let him tie all of it between its horns?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new challenge on top of the answer in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: Keeping half the strip on the rock.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the strip should be on the goat, putting all of it there would be better.

steps.title: The goat may turn its head and hide the strip
steps.stepSummary: The goat sometimes lowers or turns its head, so the sender could not see whether the strip turned white.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes it bends its head down, and he will not notice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the strip on the goat may be hidden from view, so half must stay on the rock where it can always be seen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each half does its own job. The half on the goat keeps the sender focused on pushing it. The half on the rock stays still and visible, so he can see the sign of forgiveness.
steps.whatToRemember: The strip is split for two reasons. The goat half keeps the sender focused on pushing the goat. The rock half stays visible so he can see it turn white.

phrases.english: Sometimes it bends down its head,
and he will not be aware of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 and completes the explanation of the split strip.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tying it all on the horns would be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rock half guarantees the whitening can always be seen.

steps.title: The history of where the red strip was tied
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records three stages: first the strip was tied outside the אולם, then inside, and finally half on the rock and half between the goat's horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: At first they tied the red strip on the outside of the entrance to the אולם. If it turned white, people were happy. If it did not, they were sad and embarrassed. So the חכמים arranged to tie it on the inside of the entrance. People still peeked to see it. If it turned white, they were happy, and if not, they were sad. So the חכמים arranged to tie half of it on the rock and half between the goat's horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the background to the arrangement it just discussed: half the strip on the rock and half between the horns. It explains that this setup came last, after two earlier ways of doing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for each change was emotional, not technical. When people could see the strip and it stayed red, they felt their sins were not forgiven and were ashamed. Moving the strip out to the מדבר meant nobody in the מקדש could see it on יום כיפור itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The entrance of the Entrance Hall of the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the reasons. In steps 13–16, the גמרא explained why the strip was split between the rock and the horns rather than placed entirely on one. This ברייתא explains why the strip was moved out of the מקדש at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the 'final stage' arrangement found in the משנה. The rule developed over time to protect the people's feelings on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
At first they would tie
a strip of red wool
on the entrance of the Entrance Hall, on the outside.
If it turned white, they would rejoice.
If it did not turn white, they would be sad and ashamed.
They enacted that they should tie it
on the entrance of the Entrance Hall, on the inside.
And still they would peek and look:
if it turned white, they would rejoice;
if it did not turn white, they would be sad.
So they enacted that they should tie it
half on the rock and half between its horns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the historical background for the rock-and-horns arrangement discussed in steps 13–16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The strip was moved from outside the אולם, to inside, and finally to the rock and horns, so that people would not be saddened when it failed to whiten.

steps.title: A different tradition: the strip hung inside and whitened when the goat reached the wilderness
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחום בר פפא, quoting רבי אלעזר הקפר, says the strip was originally tied inside the אולם. It turned white when the goat reached the מדבר, which showed that its מצוה had been done.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחום בר פפא said in the name of רבי אלעזר הקפר: At first they tied the red strip on the inside of the entrance to the אולם. Once the goat reached the wilderness, the strip would turn white, and they knew that its מצוה had been carried out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second tradition about where the strip was first tied. This one starts with the strip inside the אולם and focuses on the strip as a sign that the goat's מצוה was complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא began with the strip outside. רבי אלעזר הקפר begins with it inside and says nothing about people being sad. For him, the whitening was a signal in the מקדש that the goat had arrived in the מדבר and the מצוה was finished.

keyTerms.meaning: Its מצוה has been carried out

phrases.english: Rabbi Nachum bar Pappa said
in the name of Rabbi Elazar HaKappar:
At first they would tie
a strip of red wool
on the entrance of the Entrance Hall, on the inside,
and once the goat reached the wilderness
it would turn white,
and they knew that its מצוה had been done.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי נַחוּם בַּר פָּפָּא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a parallel tradition that differs from the ברייתא about where the strip was first tied and what its purpose was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Originally the strip hung inside the אולם, and its whitening showed that the goat had reached the מדבר and its מצוה was done.

steps.title: The verse hinting at the strip turning white
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'Though your sins be like scarlet, they will become white as snow' supports the idea that red turning white is a sign of forgiveness.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'If your sins are like scarlet, they will become white like snow.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר הקפר's statement continues with a פסוק from ישעיה. The פסוק supports his idea that the strip turning white shows atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the color red to sin and the color white to forgiveness. This gives a scriptural hint for why the strip's change of color was understood as a sign of כפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)
They will become white as snow

steps.whatToRemember: The red strip turning white was understood as a sign of כפרה, based on ישעיה: 'כשנים כשלג ילבינו'.

phrases.english: As it is said:
"If your sins are like scarlet,
they will become white as snow."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides scriptural support for רבי אלעזר הקפר's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That the red strip turning white signals atonement

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the goat did not reach halfway down
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה: the goat was torn apart before it reached halfway down the mountain.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'It did not reach halfway down the mountain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה to set up a new question. Nothing is being decided yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that the goat was broken into pieces almost immediately after being pushed. This fact raises a new issue: what is the status of the goat's broken limbs?

phrases.english: It would not reach halfway down the mountain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion of the red strip and opens a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The goat was torn apart before it reached halfway down the mountain.

steps.title: May one benefit from the goat's limbs?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים asked whether it is permitted to benefit from the limbs of the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Those limbs, what is their status? May one benefit from them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a real question to which it does not know the answer. Is it allowed to get any use (הנאה) from the goat's limbs after it has died?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goat was set aside for a holy מצוה, so its remains might be forbidden like other sacred items. On the other hand, it is not a קרבן brought on the מזבח, so perhaps there is no prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them (a genuine question)

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
Those limbs,
what is their status regarding benefit?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: אוֹתָן אֵבָרִים מַה הֵן בַּהֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the status of the limbs mentioned in the משנה line just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may benefit from the limbs of the שעיר המשתלח

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל argue about this. One says the limbs are permitted for benefit, and the other says they are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל disagree. One said they are permitted, and the other said they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is a dispute. It records that two great אמוראים disagree, without telling us which one holds which view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No single answer is given. Instead, the question becomes an argument between רב and שמואל, and the גמרא will now explain the reasoning behind each side.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel disagree.
One said: they are permitted,
and one said: they are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל חַד אָמַר מוּתָּרִין וְחַד אָמַר אֲסוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question by recording a dispute between אמוראים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a dispute: one אמורא permits benefit and the other forbids it.

steps.title: Beginning the reasoning of the view that permits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain the reasoning of the one who permits benefit from the limbs. The explanation continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said they are permitted...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting to explain why one opinion permits benefit from the limbs, and the actual reason comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line opens the explanation of the dispute, starting with the lenient side. Wait for the next passage to see the source or logic behind it.

phrases.english: The one who said they are permitted,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the reasoning behind the first side of the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup line: introduces the reasoning of the view that permits benefit (the reasoning continues on the next עמוד).
